correctness.rationale: The fixed source list has 24 cubic vertices and 36 edges. Independent compiled C++ with a direct closed-neighborhood algorithm enumerated all C(24,6)+C(24,7)=480700 candidate small dominating sets (none), 1767 size-eight dominators, every C(36,4)=58905 four-edge deletion (minimum 5 surviving eight-sets), and all C(36,5)=376992 five-edge deletions: exactly 276 kill every size-eight dominator. Each winner contains at least one entire three-edge incident vertex star; 36 winners have two, every vertex has exactly 13 extensions. Separately constructed networkx graph automorphisms (48) and their action on all 276 independently determined eight orbits 12,24,24,24,48,48,48,48 and all claimed representatives. Checked all eight printed nine-vertex domination witnesses by recomputing the surviving edges; the orbit action transports each witness, giving γ(T-F)=9 for every winner. This is an exhaustive finite certificate, not a sampling argument.

originality.rationale: Srivastava, arxiv:2609.02477v1 Theorem 1, proves only γ(T)=8 and b(T)=5 by one five-edge witness and exhaustive absence of four-edge winners. Its full text gives exactly 1767 domination-eight sets, but nowhere counts all 276 five-edge minima nor specifies eight symmetry orbits, thirteen local extensions or a universal post-deletion γ=9. Those extra natural equality-case assertions are not logical consequences of scalar bondage number five. Nearby Resultary findings on the same truncated octahedron compute unrelated independence complexes, not bondage-minimizer census.
residual_risks: Unindexed or later published supplementary bondage computations may independently contain the 276-minimizer list.
No classification for other cubic planar graphs follows from this single finite graph census.
